title: fix(searchBox): allow searchBox to reuse an `<input>`
body:
This no longer uses React for the `input` display (it still uses it
for the optionnal `PoweredBy` widget).

All HTML attributes already set on the `input` are kept, but sensible
defaults (like `autocorrect`, etc) are added. It listens to the
`keyup` event only to start the search.

There is no `render` method because it does not need to be updated on
results, only triggering it.

You don't handle the update of the value of the input... You can check the behaviour by using the back button : the url is updated to the previous state but the input doesn't change

![2015-09-25_15h48m44](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/10102113/0200e288-639d-11e5-9c9a-39466ad853d1.gif)

For those not experiencing the issue: here I'm trying to type `lalala` and then `labels`.
We could fix that by listening to the `helper.on('search')` and only update the value if it's different from the current query, but this feels more like a hack.
what about we expose the change event as part of the widget lifecycle? Like `searchParametersUpdate`?

I don't know. On one hand it makes sense to let widget hook themselves to the helper event as we pass the helper to them. On the other hand, we might want to control the lifecycle and group the events (as we already do with the `render` methods).

I'm still not sure on that one.

Thanks for the fix anyway, works very well now. Seems ready to be merged. If ok for you, I'll rebase+squash and push to develop.
